title: Behavioural intelligence evolved from morphogenetic problem-solving

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Behavioural intelligence evolved from morphogenetic problem-solving

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Levin proposes that behavioural intelligence in 3D space evolved from morphogenetic problem-solving competencies in anatomical space, which were themselves required by the inevitability of mutation and injury.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2024, Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue › 8. Conclusions

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Behavioral intelligence in 3D space evolved from morphogenetic problem-solving competencies in anatomical space [97,124].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Self-Improvising Memory: A Perspective on Memories as Agential, Dynamically Reinterpreting Cognitive Glue”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2024), doi:10.3390/e26060481; section “8. Conclusions”. Scope: Evolution of animals with nervous systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2024-memory-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.36

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative databases can test restricted predictions about chronology and conserved machinery. They cannot decisively recover the historical transition or distinguish direct evolutionary derivation from reuse of ancient general-purpose pathways.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Map conserved molecular and control mechanisms used in morphogenetic repair and neural behaviour across animal phylogeny, then test whether morphogenetic competencies predate and predict later behavioural-control innovations. Temporal and mechanistic continuity supports the proposal; independent origins or opposite ordering count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Shared molecules do not establish derivation of one cognitive capacity from another.

Problem-solving competency is difficult to code in ancestral taxa.

Deep evolutionary histories are reconstructed indirectly.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.25
data existence: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.4

data adequacy: 0.25

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Comparative biology can show that anatomical development precedes nervous systems. That fact does not test the specific historical claim that behavioral intelligence evolved from morphogenetic competencies. Fossils and genomes lack a variable that would separate this origin story from its rivals, so the claim is not empirically resolvable with current data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Phylogenies can order the appearance of multicellular development and of nervous systems, but that order does not distinguish derivation of behavioral intelligence from morphogenetic problem-solving from other accounts of how behavior evolved.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Earlier appearance of development than of brains is predicted by many evolutionary stories.

Morphogenetic problem-solving competency is not a character coded in comparative datasets.

The cause cited, inevitability of mutation and injury, is not a separate observable.
